newsitem.title: DUBAI: Pen portraits of Iranian presidential candidates.
newsitem.headline: Pen portraits of Iranian presidential candidates.

text.p: Following is information about the four candidates approved on Wednesday by an election screening body to run in Iran's presidential election on May 23 to succeed President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.

-- Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, 54, is parliamentary speaker and leader of a conservative group of Shi'ite Moslem clerics who have a majority in parliament together with their allies. Nateq-Nouri has been backed by key clerical groups and is close to bazaar traders, Iran's traditional merchant class. Conservative MPs have slowed Rafsanjani's market reforms, but Nateq-Nouri's backers now say he would push ahead with them if elected.

-- Mohammad Khatami, 54, is a former minister of culture and Islamic guidance known for advocating less heavy-handed social and cultural policies and regulations. He is backed by a coalition of centrists close to Rafsanjani and Islamist left-wingers who have moderated many of their views in recent years.

-- Mohammad Mohammadi Reyshahri, 51, is the official in charge of Iranian Moslems' annual haj pilgrimage to Saudi Arabia. A former intelligence (internal security) minister, he is known for his hardline conservative views, advocating closer adherence to the principles of Iran's 1979 Islamic revolution.

-- Reza Zavarei, 59, is running on his record as a top state administrator, including his current post of deputy head of the judiciary. Zavarei is the only one of the four candidates who is not a cleric. All four are Shi'ite Moslems.
Nateq-Nouri and Khatami are considered the front-runners.
